# T10 Patient Search Results

**String search defaults (R4):** A plain string search matches when the target starts with the search value. It ignores case and accents. It applies to any part of the name element: for `name`, that is family, given, prefix, suffix and text. This server also splits family names into parts on spaces and hyphens. `:contains` matches anywhere in the string. `:exact` requires a full match and is sensitive to case and accents.

**Token search defaults:** `system|code` matches one specific system and value. A bare `code` matches that value in any system. `:of-type` takes `typeSystem|typeCode|value` and matches the identifier's type together with its value.

- **q1 `name=munoz`**
  - p-01 matches: "Muñoz" folds to "munoz".
  - p-07 matches through its old name "Munoz". Every HumanName is searched, including old names.
- **q2 `family=quinones`**
  - p-02 matches. "Carreño Quiñones" splits into the part "Quiñones", which starts with "quinones" once accents are ignored.
- **q3 `given=eve`** (starts with "eve")
  - p-03 matches (Eve), as do p-04 (Evelyn), p-09 (EVE) and p-10 (Eve).
  - p-05 "Séverine" does not match because it starts with "sev".
  - p-08 does not match because "Eve" is its family name, not its given name.
- **q4 `given:contains=eve`**
  - Matches everything q3 matched.
  - Also matches p-05: "Séverine" folds to "severine", which contains "eve".
- **q5 `given:exact=Eve`**
  - p-03 and p-10 match.
  - p-09 "EVE" does not match because `:exact` is case-sensitive.
- **q6 `name=jon`**
  - p-03 matches: the family part "Jones" comes from splitting "Smith-Jones".
  - p-06 matches through "Jones".
  - p-08 matches through its given name "Jon".
  - p-05 "Johansson" does not match.
- **q7 `family:exact=Smith`**
  - p-10 matches.
  - p-03 matches because the server searches family names by their parts for the `family` parameter, and the part "Smith" is an exact match.
  - p-09 "SMITH" and p-04 "Smithers" do not match.
- **q8 hospital MRN `|000123`**
  - p-01 matches.
  - p-02 has the value "123". Token values are compared exactly, so it does not match.
  - p-03 has the same value but a different system.
- **q9 `identifier=000123`** (any system)
  - p-01 and p-03 match.
  - p-06 also matches through its driver's licence identifier, which has the value 000123.
- **q10 `:of-type` MR|000123**
  - p-01 and p-03 match.
  - p-06's 000123 identifier has the type DL, not MR, so it does not match.
- **q11 `name=dr&gender=male`**
  - p-06 matches: its prefix "Dr." starts with "dr" and its gender is male.

[organization policy reminder removed]

```json
{
  "q1": ["Patient/p-01", "Patient/p-07"],
  "q2": ["Patient/p-02"],
  "q3": ["Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-04", "Patient/p-09", "Patient/p-10"],
  "q4": ["Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-04", "Patient/p-05", "Patient/p-09", "Patient/p-10"],
  "q5": ["Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-10"],
  "q6": ["Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-06", "Patient/p-08"],
  "q7": ["Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-10"],
  "q8": ["Patient/p-01"],
  "q9": ["Patient/p-01", "Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-06"],
  "q10": ["Patient/p-01", "Patient/p-03"],
  "q11": ["Patient/p-06"]
}
```

**Assumptions** (per the server rules and FHIR R4 string semantics):
- Default string matching is case-insensitive, accent-insensitive, and starts-with.
- `:contains` matches anywhere in the value. `:exact` is case-sensitive and matches the whole value.
- Family values are also matched by their parts (split on spaces and hyphens), even with `:exact`.
- `name` searches family, given, prefix, suffix, and text of every HumanName, regardless of `use` or `period`.
- Token matching is exact on system and code/value, with no normalization.

**Per query**

- **q1 `name=munoz`**: p-01 family "Muñoz" matches after accent folding. p-07's old-name family "Munoz" matches because `name` ignores `use` and `period`. p-02's text does not start with "munoz".
- **q2 `family=quinones`**: p-02 family "Carreño Quiñones" splits into parts, and "Quiñones" folds to "quinones".
- **q3 `given=eve`**: starts-with on given only. Matches p-03 "Eve", p-04 "Evelyn", p-09 "EVE" (case-insensitive), and p-10 "Eve". p-08's family is "Eve", but `given` does not search family, so it is excluded. p-05 "Séverine" does not start with "eve".
- **q4 `given:contains=eve`**: anywhere in given. Adds p-05 "Séverine" (contains "eve") and p-06 "Steve". p-08 is still excluded because its given name is "Jon".
- **q5 `given:exact=Eve`**: case-sensitive whole-value match. Only p-03 and p-10. p-09 "EVE" fails the case check, and p-04 "Evelyn" is not an exact match.
- **q6 `name=jon`**: p-08 given "Jon". p-06 family "Jones" starts with "jon".
- **q7 `family:exact=Smith`**: p-10 "Smith" matches. p-03's family "Smith-Jones" matches through its part "Smith". p-09 "SMITH" fails the case check. "Smithers" is not equal to "Smith".
- **q8 `identifier=<hospital system>|000123`**: only p-01. p-03 uses the clinic system. p-06's 000123 is a DL identifier with a different system.
- **q9 `identifier=000123`**: any system. p-01, p-03, and p-06 (its DL identifier also has value 000123).
- **q10 `identifier:of-type=v2-0203|MR|000123`**: p-01 and p-03 have MR identifiers with value 000123. p-06's 000123 is typed DL, so it is excluded.
- **q11 `name=dr&gender=male`**: p-06's prefix "Dr." starts with "dr". Punctuation is not stripped, but starts-with still matches. p-06 is male. No other patient has a name starting with "dr".

[organization policy reminder removed]

```json
{"q1": ["Patient/p-01", "Patient/p-07"], "q2": ["Patient/p-02"], "q3": ["Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-04", "Patient/p-09", "Patient/p-10"], "q4": ["Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-04", "Patient/p-05", "Patient/p-06", "Patient/p-09", "Patient/p-10"], "q5": ["Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-10"], "q6": ["Patient/p-06", "Patient/p-08"], "q7": ["Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-10"], "q8": ["Patient/p-01"], "q9": ["Patient/p-01", "Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-06"], "q10": ["Patient/p-01", "Patient/p-03"], "q11": ["Patient/p-06"]}
```

Default string searches match prefixes and ignore case and accents. `:contains` matches substrings; `:exact` preserves case and accents. All names participate, including old names and prefixes, and family-name parts are searchable.

Identifier values preserve leading zeros. An unqualified identifier matches across systems; `:of-type` also requires the specified identifier type.

```json
{
  "q1": ["Patient/p-01", "Patient/p-07"],
  "q2": ["Patient/p-02"],
  "q3": ["Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-04", "Patient/p-09", "Patient/p-10"],
  "q4": ["Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-04", "Patient/p-05", "Patient/p-06", "Patient/p-09", "Patient/p-10"],
  "q5": ["Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-10"],
  "q6": ["Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-06", "Patient/p-08"],
  "q7": ["Patient/p-10"],
  "q8": ["Patient/p-01"],
  "q9": ["Patient/p-01", "Patient/p-03", "Patient/p-06"],
  "q10": ["Patient/p-01", "Patient/p-03"],
  "q11": ["Patient/p-06"]
}
```

## Per-query analysis

**Key points used throughout**
- The server does not filter on Observation status, so `o-6` (`entered-in-error`) still matches searches on its code and value.
- Value searches with no unit match on the number alone, so `o-4` (250 mg/dL) counts for `gt9`.
- Each `_has` parameter is evaluated independently, so two `_has` parameters can be satisfied by different Observations. A composite parameter requires both components to match the same Observation.
- `_include` and `_revinclude` are applied once to the match set and are not recursive.
- `o-8` references `Patient/pt-9`, which is not on the server.

**q1: `_has` code AND `_has` value-quantity (independent)**
- Patients with a 4548-4 Observation: pt-1 (o-1), pt-2 (o-3), pt-3 (o-5), pt-5 (o-6). pt-9 is absent.
- Patients with any Observation value > 9: pt-1 (o-1, o-2), pt-2 (o-4, 250), pt-3 (o-5), pt-5 (o-6, o-7). pt-4 is excluded (max 95).
- Intersection: pt-1, pt-2, pt-3, pt-5. pt-2 matches through different Observations (o-3 for code, o-4 for value).

**q2: composite `code-value-quantity` (same Observation)**
- Observations with 4548-4 and value > 9: o-1 (9.5), o-5 (9.2), o-6 (10.1). o-8 (11.0) is on pt-9, which is not a Patient on the server, so it does not affect this result. o-3 (7.0) fails.
- Patients: pt-1, pt-3, pt-5.

**q3: q2 AND `_has` status=final**
- The status `_has` is a separate, independent condition. pt-1 (o-1), pt-3 (o-5), and pt-5 (o-7 is final) each have a final Observation.
- Result: pt-1, pt-3, pt-5.

**q4: composite Observation search with `patient.gender=female`**
- Composite matches: o-1, o-5, o-6, o-8. o-8's subject does not exist, so the chain fails.
- Female subjects: o-1 (pt-1), o-5 (pt-3). o-6 (pt-5) is male.
- Result: o-1, o-5.

**q5: composite Observation search with `_include=Observation:patient`**
- Matches: o-1, o-5, o-6, o-8. The composite search does not check the subject, so o-8 is included in the match set.
- Includes: pt-1, pt-3, pt-5. pt-9 is not on the server, so nothing is included for o-8.

**q6: `patient=pt-2` with `_revinclude=Provenance:target`**
- Matches: o-3, o-4.
- Provenance targeting these: prov-2 (targets o-3 and o-4). prov-1 targets o-1 and is not included.

**q7: `_has` code AND gender=female, with two `_revinclude`s**
- Patients with a 4548-4 Observation: pt-1, pt-2, pt-3, pt-5. Female: pt-1, pt-3.
- `Provenance:target` reverse-includes provenance whose target is a matched Patient: prov-3 (targets pt-1). prov-1 targets o-1, which is not in the match set, so it is not included.
- `Observation:patient` reverse-includes Observations of the matched patients: pt-1 gives o-1 and o-2; pt-3 gives o-5.
- The includes are not followed further, so prov-1 is not added via o-1.

[organization policy reminder removed]

```json
{
  "q1": ["Patient/pt-1", "Patient/pt-2", "Patient/pt-3", "Patient/pt-5"],
  "q2": ["Patient/pt-1", "Patient/pt-3", "Patient/pt-5"],
  "q3": ["Patient/pt-1", "Patient/pt-3", "Patient/pt-5"],
  "q4": ["Observation/o-1", "Observation/o-5"],
  "q5": {
    "match": ["Observation/o-1", "Observation/o-5", "Observation/o-6", "Observation/o-8"],
    "include": ["Patient/pt-1", "Patient/pt-3", "Patient/pt-5"]
  },
  "q6": {
    "match": ["Observation/o-3", "Observation/o-4"],
    "include": ["Provenance/prov-2"]
  },
  "q7": {
    "match": ["Patient/pt-1", "Patient/pt-3"],
    "include": ["Observation/o-1", "Observation/o-2", "Observation/o-5", "Provenance/prov-3"]
  }
}
```

Separate component parameters can match different components of the same Observation. A composite requires its code and quantity to match within the same component. Comma-separated composites are OR; repeated parameters are AND.

For quantity comparisons, `ge` and `gt` use the stated numeric boundary, so 139.6 fails `ge140` and 89.6 fails `ge90`. Equality `$140` uses the implicit range [139.5, 140.5), matching both 140 and 139.6.

- **q1:** Every panel has a diastolic code and some component quantity ≥90. This includes `bp-06`, whose systolic value satisfies the quantity condition.
- **q2:** Requires a diastolic value ≥90 in that same component.
- **q3:** Requires either elevated component and `final` status.
- **q4:** Requires both elevated components.
- **q5:** Matches systolic values within the equality range for 140.
- **q6:** Matches the standalone systolic Observation’s top-level code and value.
- **q7:** Searches only top-level values. Without units specified, both heart rate 98 and standalone systolic 152 match.

```json
{
  "q1": ["Observation/bp-01", "Observation/bp-02", "Observation/bp-03", "Observation/bp-04", "Observation/bp-05", "Observation/bp-06", "Observation/bp-07", "Observation/bp-08", "Observation/bp-09"],
  "q2": ["Observation/bp-02", "Observation/bp-04", "Observation/bp-07", "Observation/bp-08"],
  "q3": ["Observation/bp-01", "Observation/bp-02", "Observation/bp-04", "Observation/bp-06", "Observation/bp-07"],
  "q4": ["Observation/bp-04", "Observation/bp-07"],
  "q5": ["Observation/bp-07", "Observation/bp-09"],
  "q6": ["Observation/sbp-01"],
  "q7": ["Observation/hr-01", "Observation/sbp-01"]
}
```

**Key interpretation points**

- **Separate `_has` parameters are ANDed independently.** Each one can be satisfied by a different Observation. Only a composite parameter binds `code` and `value` to the same Observation.
- **`value-quantity=gt9` means value > 9.** This follows the R4 number semantics, where `gt100` means "greater than 100". No unit is given, so values in any unit match. The server's "range above starts at END" rule applies only to date prefixes, not quantities.
- **`gt9` matches every Observation except o-3 (7.0).** The matches are o-1 (9.5), o-2 (100), o-4 (250), o-5 (9.2), o-6 (10.1), o-7 (130), o-8 (11.0) and o-9 (95).
- **`status` is not filtered unless the query asks for it.** o-6 is `entered-in-error` but still matches searches with no `status` criterion.
- **o-8 points to Patient/pt-9, which is not on the server.** It can match direct Observation searches. It cannot make any Patient match, cannot satisfy the chained `patient.gender`, and its patient cannot be included.

**q1**
- The HbA1c (4548-4) condition matches pt-1 (o-1), pt-2 (o-3), pt-3 (o-5) and pt-5 (o-6).
- The value > 9 condition matches pt-1, pt-2 (via o-4), pt-3, pt-4 and pt-5.
- The intersection is pt-1, pt-2, pt-3 and pt-5.
- pt-2 matches only because two different Observations satisfy the two conditions.

**q2**
- The composite requires one Observation with HbA1c > 9. That gives o-1, o-5, o-6 and o-8.
- Mapped to patients on the server, the result is pt-1, pt-3 and pt-5.

**q3**
- Start from the q2 set.
- The separate `status=final` condition can be met by any final Observation for the patient. pt-1 (o-1), pt-3 (o-5) and pt-5 (o-7) all qualify.
- pt-5 stays in even though o-6 is entered-in-error.

**q4**
- The HbA1c > 9 Observations are o-1, o-5, o-6 and o-8.
- The female filter keeps o-1 (pt-1) and o-5 (pt-3).
- o-6 drops out because pt-5 is male. o-8 drops out because pt-9 cannot be resolved.

**q5**
- The matches are o-1, o-5, o-6 and o-8.
- The included patients are pt-1, pt-3 and pt-5. pt-9 does not exist, so nothing is included for o-8.

**q6**
- The matches are o-3 and o-4.
- The revinclude adds prov-2.

**q7**
- Patients with an HbA1c Observation are pt-1, pt-2, pt-3 and pt-5. The female ones are pt-1 and pt-3.
- `_revinclude=Provenance:target` adds prov-3, which targets pt-1.
- `_revinclude=Observation:patient` adds o-1 and o-2 (pt-1) and o-5 (pt-3).

```json
{
  "q1": ["Patient/pt-1", "Patient/pt-2", "Patient/pt-3", "Patient/pt-5"],
  "q2": ["Patient/pt-1", "Patient/pt-3", "Patient/pt-5"],
  "q3": ["Patient/pt-1", "Patient/pt-3", "Patient/pt-5"],
  "q4": ["Observation/o-1", "Observation/o-5"],
  "q5": {"match": ["Observation/o-1", "Observation/o-5", "Observation/o-6", "Observation/o-8"], "include": ["Patient/pt-1", "Patient/pt-3", "Patient/pt-5"]},
  "q6": {"match": ["Observation/o-3", "Observation/o-4"], "include": ["Provenance/prov-2"]},
  "q7": {"match": ["Patient/pt-1", "Patient/pt-3"], "include": ["Observation/o-1", "Observation/o-2", "Observation/o-5", "Provenance/prov-3"]}
}
```

# FHIR R4 search results for task T09 (hypertension registry)

## How quantity prefixes behave on this server

- A search value like `90` has an implicit range of **[89.5, 90.5)**, based on its precision.
- `ge90` matches any target ≥ 90.5. It also matches any target that overlaps [89.5, 90.5).
- In practice, **≥ 89.5 matches `ge90`**, and **≥ 139.5 matches `ge140`**.
- So the decimal device values in bp-09 (139.6 and 89.6) match `ge140` and `ge90`.
- `gt90` matches only targets above 90.5.

## q1: separate parameters, no composite

`component-code=…|8462-4&component-value-quantity=ge90`

- The two parameters are evaluated independently. Each one can be satisfied by a *different* component of the same Observation.
- All nine BP panels have a component with code 8462-4. This includes bp-06, whose diastolic component has a code but only a dataAbsentReason.
- Every panel's systolic component is ≥ 90, so the value test always passes on systolic.
- **Result: bp-01 through bp-09.**
  - hr-01 and sbp-01 have no components, so they don't match.
  - bp-08 still appears because there is no status filter.

## q2: composite, diastolic ≥ 90 within the same component

| Resource | Diastolic | Match? |
|---|---|---|
| bp-01 | 80 | no |
| bp-02 | 95 | yes |
| bp-03 | 80 | no |
| bp-04 | 92 | yes |
| bp-05 | 88 | no (range [87.5, 88.5) does not reach 89.5) |
| bp-06 | no value (dataAbsentReason) | no |
| bp-07 | 90 | yes |
| bp-08 | 91 | yes |
| bp-09 | 89.6 | yes (inside [89.5, 90.5)) |

**Result: bp-02, bp-04, bp-07, bp-08, bp-09.**

## q3: systolic ≥ 140 OR diastolic ≥ 90, AND status=final

- Systolic ≥ 140: bp-01 (150), bp-04 (145), bp-06 (160), bp-07 (140), bp-09 (139.6).
- Diastolic ≥ 90: bp-02, bp-04, bp-07, bp-08, bp-09.
- The union is bp-01, 02, 04, 06, 07, 08, 09.
- Removing bp-08 (status entered-in-error) leaves **bp-01, bp-02, bp-04, bp-06, bp-07, bp-09.**

## q4: systolic ≥ 140 AND diastolic ≥ 90

- This is the intersection of the two sets above: **bp-04, bp-07, bp-09.**
- bp-06 drops out because its diastolic component has no value.

## q5: systolic eq 140

- `140` means the range [139.5, 140.5).
- bp-07 (140) and bp-09 (139.6) both fall inside it.
- **Result: bp-07, bp-09.**

## q6: code-value-quantity with systolic code

- This parameter only looks at Observation.code and Observation.valueQuantity at the top level.
- The panels have top-level code 85354-9 and no valueQuantity, so they don't match.
- **Result: sbp-01 only** (152).

## q7: value-quantity gt90

- No code is specified, so any Observation with a top-level valueQuantity above 90.5 matches.
- hr-01 (98 beats/min) and sbp-01 (152 mmHg) both match.
- Including the heart rate is a registry pitfall: the query is not restricted to blood pressure.
- **Result: hr-01, sbp-01.**

## Takeaways for the registry

- **q1 is broken:** it flags every panel. Use the composite form (q2/q3) so the code and value are tested on the same component.
- **Decimals near the threshold match:** values like 139.6 and 89.6 match `ge140` and `ge90` because of implicit precision ranges. If that is not intended, write the threshold with more precision (e.g. `ge140.0`) so the matching range is narrower.
- **Standalone systolic Observations are missed:** composite component searches don't find sbp-01. Add a `code-value-quantity` query (q6) to catch it.

```json
{
  "q1": ["Observation/bp-01", "Observation/bp-02", "Observation/bp-03", "Observation/bp-04", "Observation/bp-05", "Observation/bp-06", "Observation/bp-07", "Observation/bp-08", "Observation/bp-09"],
  "q2": ["Observation/bp-02", "Observation/bp-04", "Observation/bp-07", "Observation/bp-08", "Observation/bp-09"],
  "q3": ["Observation/bp-01", "Observation/bp-02", "Observation/bp-04", "Observation/bp-06", "Observation/bp-07", "Observation/bp-09"],
  "q4": ["Observation/bp-04", "Observation/bp-07", "Observation/bp-09"],
  "q5": ["Observation/bp-07", "Observation/bp-09"],
  "q6": ["Observation/sbp-01"],
  "q7": ["Observation/hr-01", "Observation/sbp-01"]
}
```

[organization policy reminder removed]

**Key points**

- `component-code` and `component-value-quantity` in q1 are separate parameters, so they match independently. The code match can come from the DBP component and the value match from the SBP component.
- Composite parameters (q2, q3, q5) must match on the same component. Separate composite parameters (q4) match independently.
- `ge90` uses the implicit range [89.5, 90.5), so 89.6 matches. `ge140` uses [139.5, 140.5), so 139.6 matches. `eq140` also matches 139.6.
- `code-value-quantity` and `value-quantity` look only at top-level `code`/`valueQuantity`, never at components.
- Nothing filters on status by default, so `entered-in-error` bp-08 is returned unless `status=final` is added.

**Per query**

- **q1:** Every panel has a DBP component with code 8462-4, and every panel has an SBP component ≥ 90. The independent match makes all nine panels match, including bp-03 (120/80) and bp-05 (135/88), which are not above goal. bp-06 matches on the code alone. hr-01 and sbp-01 have no components, so they do not match.
- **q2:** Same-component DBP ≥ 90 (with overlap): bp-02 (95), bp-04 (92), bp-07 (90), bp-08 (91, not status-filtered), bp-09 (89.6 overlaps 90). bp-06 has no DBP value.
- **q3:** The comma makes the two composites an OR. Matching components are SBP ≥ 140 (bp-01, bp-04, bp-06, bp-07, bp-09) or DBP ≥ 90 (bp-02, bp-04, bp-07, bp-08, bp-09). `status=final` removes bp-08.
- **q4:** Two separate composites (AND). SBP ≥ 140 set ∩ DBP ≥ 90 set = bp-04, bp-07, bp-09.
- **q5:** Same-component eq 140 with overlap: SBP 140 (bp-07) and 139.6 (bp-09). The `eq` prefix doesn't check the sign of the difference, so it matches both sides of 140.
- **q6:** Only sbp-01 has top-level code 8480-6, with value 152. Panel components do not count.
- **q7:** `value-quantity` checks top-level values only. hr-01 (98) and sbp-01 (152) are > 90. No unit filter is applied, so the unit does not matter.

**Caveat on bp-09 (139.6/89.6):** These matches depend on the overlap rule. Under strict comparison (v ≥ 90 or v ≥ 140), bp-09 drops out of q2, q3, q4, and q5. Clinically, 139.6 and 89.6 are below the thresholds, so the registry should decide on decimal handling explicitly rather than rely on this behaviour.

**Registry recommendations**

- Use the same-component composite (q3) for the "above goal" criterion, and add `status=final`.
- Decide how decimal readings are compared to thresholds.
- Exclude bp-06, where the DBP has only a dataAbsentReason.
- Handle the standalone systolic (sbp-01) with a separate query, because it is not a panel component.

```json
{"q1": ["Observation/bp-01","Observation/bp-02","Observation/bp-03","Observation/bp-04","Observation/bp-05","Observation/bp-06","Observation/bp-07","Observation/bp-08","Observation/bp-09"], "q2": ["Observation/bp-02","Observation/bp-04","Observation/bp-07","Observation/bp-08","Observation/bp-09"], "q3": ["Observation/bp-01","Observation/bp-02","Observation/bp-04","Observation/bp-06","Observation/bp-07","Observation/bp-09"], "q4": ["Observation/bp-04","Observation/bp-07","Observation/bp-09"], "q5": ["Observation/bp-07","Observation/bp-09"], "q6": ["Observation/sbp-01"], "q7": ["Observation/hr-01","Observation/sbp-01"]}
```
